Korean: 가: 목이 부어서 아파요. / 나: 말을 많이 하지 말고 따뜻한 물을 자주 드세요.
English: A: My throat is swollen so it hurts. / B: Don't talk too much but frequently drink warm water.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action verb when giving a command or suggestion to not do a certain action mentioned first but instead do the action mentioned later.

Korean: 가: 결혼식에 입고 갈 정장이 없어서 사야 할 것 같아요. / 나: 잠깐 입을 건데 사지 말고 빌리세요.
English: A: I don't have a suit to wear to the wedding, so I think I have to buy one. / B: You'll only wear it once so don't buy it. Just borrow a suit.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action verb when giving a command or suggestion to not do a certain action mentioned first but instead do the action mentioned later.

Korean: 열이 많이 납니다. 그리고 기침도 심합니다.
English: I have a high fever. And my cough is also severe.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 다음 주에 동창회를 할 거예요. 그러니까 꼭 오세요.
English: We are having an alumnus meeting next week so please come.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 비빔냉면을 다 못 먹었다. 왜냐하면 너무 매웠기 때문이다.
English: I couldn't finish eating the bibim-naengmyeon because it was too spicy.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 친구와 콘서트를 보러 갔다. 그러나 남은 표가 없어서 그냥 집으로 돌아와야 했다.
English: I went to see a concert with my friend. But because there were no more tickets left, we had to just come back home.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 가: 여행을 가고 싶지요? / 나: 네, 그렇지만 시간이 없어요.
English: A: You want to go on a trip, don't you? / B: Yes, but I don't have time.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 가: 너무 피곤해서 그냥 자고 싶어요. / 나: 그래도 씻고 주무세요.
English: A: I am so tired that I just want to go to sleep. / B: You should still wash up and then go to sleep.
Grammar Notes: This is a word that connects two sentences.

Korean: 호텔은 제가 예약할 테니까 유키 씨는 렌터카를 예약해 주세요.
English: I'll make the reservations for the hotel, so Yuki, please make the reservations for the rental car.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.

Korean: 제가 김밥을 만들어 올 테니까 흐엉 씨는 음료수를 준비해 주세요.
English: I'll make the gimbap and come, so Huang, please prepare the drinks.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.

Korean: 주말에는 극장에 사람이 많을 테니까 평일에 가세요.
English: There will be many people at the theater on the weekends so go on the weekday.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.

Korean: 지금 가면 차가 밀릴 테니까 지하철로 갑시다.
English: If we go now there will be traffic, so let's take the subway.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.

Korean: 가: 잠깐만 기다려 주시겠어요? / 나: 네, 커피를 마시면서 기다릴 테니까 천천히 오세요.
English: A: Can you wait for a little while? / B: Yes. I'll be waiting while I drink coffee so take your time.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.

Korean: 가: 지금 밤 11시인데 노라 씨에게 전화해도 될까요? / 나: 지금은 노라 씨가 자고 있을 테니까 내일 전화하세요.
English: A: It's 11 o'clock at night right now but is it okay to call Nora? / B: Nora will be sleeping so call her tomorrow.
Grammar Notes: This is used with an action or descriptive verb when connecting an uncompleted work as the reason for the following sentence.
